metadata.title: Storage Access & Mediation Pattern
metadata.remarks: Defines how access to stored data is explicitly mediated, scoped, and authorized by storage platforms, preventing implicit or inherited authority from applications, automation, or administrative context.

props.name: capability
props.remarks: Business capability responsible for governing who may access institutional information assets and under what conditions.

props.name: technology-domain
props.remarks: Persistent storage technologies providing block, file, object, and virtualized access mechanisms.

props.name: technology-domain
props.remarks: Technologies that enforce identity-based access decisions for services, systems, and data.

props.name: architecture-pattern
props.remarks: Establishes explicit mediation between identities and platform services to prevent implicit trust and authority inheritance.

props.name: data-domain
props.remarks: Information assets that require governed and auditable access controls.

props.name: data-domain
props.remarks: Data whose confidentiality and access must be strictly controlled due to risk or regulatory considerations.

props.name: nist-guidance
props.remarks: Defines data-centric access mediation principles, role separation, and enforcement of policy independent of application logic.

components.title: Explicit Access Mediation
components.description: Ensures all access to storage resources occurs through explicit, policy-enforced mediation points rather than implicit trust paths.

props.name: attack-tactics
props.remarks: Initial access and persistence often exploit direct or implicitly trusted access paths.

props.name: attack-techniques
props.remarks: Valid account abuse and privilege escalation rely on unmediated access.

props.name: defensive-techniques
props.remarks: Centralizes and enforces access control through explicit mediation.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Access to storage resources is explicitly enforced.
Remote and programmatic storage access is mediated and controlled.

components.title: Identity Role Separation
components.description: Separates identities used for human access, application access, automation, and platform administration to prevent authority collapse.

props.name: attack-tactics
props.remarks: Over-privileged or shared identities are prime targets for credential compromise.

props.name: attack-techniques
props.remarks: Credential dumping and token reuse exploit role overlap.

props.name: defensive-techniques
props.remarks: Prevents lateral authority inheritance across identities.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Unique identification is enforced for all storage access.
Separation of duties is enforced between storage administration and data access.

components.title: Least-Privilege Object Access
components.description: Restricts access to specific data objects, operations, and contexts rather than broad storage scopes.

props.name: attack-tactics
props.remarks: Excessive read or write privileges enable silent data collection.

props.name: attack-techniques
props.remarks: Collection from network and cloud storage relies on broad permissions.

props.name: defensive-techniques
props.remarks: Minimizes accessible data scope per identity and operation.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Least privilege is enforced for storage access.
Fine-grained object-level access restrictions are applied.

components.title: Automation Access Guardrails
components.description: Explicitly constrains automation access to prevent pipelines, scripts, and tools from becoming implicit data owners.

props.name: attack-tactics
props.remarks: Automation misuse can directly destroy or exfiltrate data.

props.name: attack-techniques
props.remarks: Destructive automation inhibits data availability and recovery.

props.name: defensive-techniques
props.remarks: Prevents automation from exceeding authorized access scope.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Automation is limited to explicitly required functionality.
Automation identities are managed and reviewed.
